name: Pam (Cameroon)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only a sociolinguistic survey (Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai, Oblo) and comparative Adamawa work in Glottolog; no descriptive phonology of Pam found.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record pamm1242 (Hammarström et al.), with reference records 158437 Boyd & Pasch 1988, 29992 Elders 2006, 569683 Campbell et al. 2022 (ElCat), 65008 Bennett 1983

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. (2013 Wayback capture). Adamawa language list (classification table).
sources.note: Nothing; Pam is not even listed (Northern Mbum group shows only Dama, Ndai (Galke)/Pormi, Kali).

sources.citation: Elders, Stefan. 2006. Issues in comparative Kebi-Benue (Adamawa). Africana Linguistica 12: 37-88.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent for Pam or any Kebi-Benue language (only 'it should be stressed' phrases). Pam data are Boyd's 1974 wordlist ('his data are mostly from Pam', p. 51); Pam/Mono discussed for glottal stop (p. 49), loss of prenasalisation (table 10, p. 51), schwa, a- preformative. Tone section 3.4 (pp. 58-59) quotes Boyd 1989a: 202-203 second-hand: Southern Mbum languages have two tone levels, 'the remaining subgroups have three'; Elders adds 'The transcription of tone in Boyd's word lists has to be checked.' Persée landing page fetched sources; PDF endpoint altcha-protected, so the full…

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2002. Sociolinguistic language survey of Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai, and Oblo. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-048. Dallas: SIL International. 12 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Rapid-appraisal sociolinguistic survey (June 2001); 126-word CREA wordlists were recorded but are not printed; no phonology, no mention of stress, accent or tone in any of the 12 pages (grep 0 hits). Pam section (3.2.4, pp. 6-7) is demographic only; Appendix A reprints the Ethnologue and ALCAM [361] entries.

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2001. Unpublished 126-word CREA wordlists and recordings of Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai (SIL Cameroon survey department archive).

sources.note: The survey report says the wordlists were transcribed and recorded 'to document their existence'; the transcriptions would show whether the surveyors marked tone or stress on Pam words.

sources.note: The only primary Pam data in print (Glottolog MED): comparative wordlist with tone-marked Pam forms and a phonological inventory (p. 16 on the Pam/Mono data, p. 23 consonants, p. 25 glottal stop, p. 57 sound changes per Elders 2006); any remark on tone vs. stress in the 'lakka' group would be here.

sources.note: Elders did fieldwork on Mono and recorded the name Kpam; his unpublished notes are the only post-1974 first-hand data on the Pam/Mono cluster and would carry his own tone (and any stress) analysis. Elders died in 2007; the Nachlass location is unknown.
